# Keys you hand over - qa-runner

## Outputs

- `work/evidence/manual/<case>/tried.md` - the exploration log of a manual window: one row per cell the runner took, with the capture that shows it; the recorder's `build` reads it for citations and never writes it

Required at your stop (stage S6): `work/run-report.json`.

## Witness

Your witness artifact (stages.json `witness`): `work/run-report.json`.

## Handoff form

Contract `s6-runner-to-analyst` (fill `work/handoffs/<dispatch>.yaml`; `handoff_check.py` reads it):

- `inputs_read[].version` (required) - its window id
- `inputs_read[].instances_handed` (required) - n
- `inputs_read[].manual_cases_handed` (required) - n
- `header.window` (required) - the block ids this dispatch ran
- `header.verdict` (required) - one of vocabulary.header_verdicts
- `run.execution_status` (required) - one of vocabulary.execution_status
- `run.witness` (required) - the run_suite summary with the exit code and the totals line
- `run.environment` (required) - the stand id
- `run.application_build` (required) - what was actually running, from the probe - not from the plan
- `run.probe_before` (required) - path of the record
- `run.probe_after` (required) - path of the record
- `run.totals` (required) - passed / failed / error / skipped / not_run, as the report counted them
- `run.window_totals` (required) - the same counts for the rows this dispatch produced
- `scope[].id` (required) - instance or case id
- `scope[].state` (required) - one of vocabulary.row_states
- `scope[].reason` (required) - a verdict of at most 80 characters - the explanation lives in the artifact
- `scope[].case` (required) - case id
- `scope[].obligations` (required) - the obligation ids it discharges
- `scope[].executed` (required) - fresh|reused|none
- `scope[].rerun_reason` (optional) - the exact fingerprint or provenance that moved, when this was rerun
- `scope[].evidence` (required) - work/evidence/... - the artifact, not the claim
- `scope[].duration` (optional) - seconds, or a dash
- `manual_observations[].case` (required) - case id
- `manual_observations[].then` (required) - the expectation, quoted from the case
- `manual_observations[].observed` (required) - what was actually seen, in the product's own terms
- `manual_observations[].before_change` (required) - the record's before_change - r, value, ref and source claim or not_recorded - as built by code; not_recorded is never read as unchanged
- `manual_observations[].result` (required) - passed|failed|inconclusive|manual_skipped
- `manual_observations[].evidence` (required) - path
- `manual_observations[].why_inconclusive` (optional) - what the observation failed to settle, when it did
- `manual_observations[].surprises` (required) - the record's surprises[] (id, step, word, kind, fact, evidence) and surprise_detection, as built by code from the recorder's lines; a line an observation cites with `surprise: <id>` is judged inside that observation, every other line is a target `<case>#sur-<id>` for the analyst (at most 30; the rest are one `<case>#sur-overflow`). surprise_detection other than `on` means the page was not fully watched: no surprise is not 'nothing happened'
- `env_blocked[].id` (required) - instance or case id
- `env_blocked[].probe_line` (required) - the env_probe check that failed, verbatim
- `env_blocked[].remedy` (required) - the exact change, by name
- `env_blocked[].owner` (required) - factory|user
- `superseded[].row` (required) - the ghost row id
- `superseded[].superseded_by` (required) - the instance id that replaced it
- `claims.every_row_carries_an_evidence_path` (required) - true|false
- `claims.every_blocked_row_names_a_remedy_and_the_probe_line` (required) - true|false
- `claims.no_comparison_was_fabricated_where_before_evidence_is_missing` (required) - true|false
- `claims.handed_and_manual_human_cases_are_absent_by_design` (required) - true|false
- `claims.the_report_was_reduced_by_code_not_written` (required) - true|false
- `tried[].requirement` (required) - the window: its case ids or its area
- `tried[].technique` (required) - what you ran in that window (the command or the steps)
- `tried[].observation` (required) - what you saw, in one line
- `tried[].evidence` (required) - the path of tried.md (and anchor) where it shows
- `tried_note` (optional) - why the table is empty, or a dash when it has rows
- `unresolved[].id` (required) - instance or case id
- `unresolved[].reason` (required) - one of vocabulary.unresolved_reasons
- `unresolved[].detail` (required) - what exactly is missing, and what would settle it
- `blocked.field` (only when blocked) - the field of this file the role cannot fill
- `blocked.problem` (only when blocked) - what the role tried and what refused it, verbatim
- `blocked.tried[]` (only when blocked) - command or step, and its answer
- `blocked.data[]` (only when blocked) - path of anything the conductor needs to see

Every handoff form shares one skeleton (`common_shape` of handoffs/index.yaml): `inputs`, `inputs_read`, `header`, `scope`, `artifacts`, `claims`, `unresolved`, `blocked`.

## What code will check of you

`<T>` is your ticket, `<ID>` your dispatch id, `<home>` the project's qa-factory folder - all three stand in your prompt (`Ticket: ... Dispatch: ...`) and in your task packet.

- [exit_gate:EG-digest-form] Your final message is the handoff form: a header `<role> <stage> <window> · ok|concerns|halt|impossible`; one line `<id> · <state> · <reason of at most 80 characters>` for every item of the dispatch's scope (a halting digest owes no scope lines); nothing but those lines between the header and the path; and, last, the task-relative path of what you wrote (a halting digest may omit it). A verdict or a state word outside the form's list is advice, not a refusal; a reason over 80 characters, an absolute path under the task root, prose before the header and a missing path the witness names are mended by code when mending makes the form pass. Door: fix the digest line the refusal names, then end the dispatch again.
- [exit_gate:EG-text-end] Your dispatch ends with the host's handback tool carrying your digest line, never with free text after it. Door: call the host's handback tool with your digest line.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-artifact-rewrite] An artifact that exists with content, and whose `artifact-writers.json` entry carries `rewrite`, is never replaced whole by Write. Door: the point edit the entry's `rewrite` names (quoted in the refusal).
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-big-read] A file over `config.read.max_bytes` is read with `offset`/`limit`, a PDF with a `pages` range within `config.read.max_pdf_pages`, and a picture only up to `config.read.max_image_bytes`. Door: `Grep -n` for the line, then Read with `offset`/`limit`; a PDF by `pages` ranges.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-case-store] When the project declares `cases_root`, a case file is written inside it and nowhere else. Door: write it as `<cases_root>/<area>/<case id>.md`.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-command-size] A Bash or PowerShell command is at most 64 KB (65,536 characters); a longer one is refused before any other check reads it. Door: split the work into several commands, or write the long text to a file with Write and name the file.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-config-write] A role never writes `qa-factory/config.json`, by Write, Edit, NotebookEdit or a shell write shape. Door: name `launch: <cause>` (or `launch: unknown`) and the evidence line in your digest.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-direct-test-run] Tests are never launched directly (any form of `launch-causes.json` `run_forms`): outside a dispatch through `run_suite.py --task <T> --label <label> -- <command>`, inside an open dispatch only through a typed request; a command that runs no test carries its runner's no-run flag. Door: `run_suite.py --mine <CASE>` (inside a dispatch); `run_suite.py --template request` prints a request skeleton.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-external-writes] No shell command writes to a tracker or a test-management system (a declared `external_writes` command, a tracker CLI with a write verb and object, or an `api` call with a write method). Door: write a proposal file under `work/proposals/` in the shape `external-writes.md` defines.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-git-config] A shell command never changes git configuration: `git config` passes only with `--get`, `--get-all`, `--get-regexp`, `--get-urlmatch`, `--list` or `-l`. Door: report the blocker in your digest; the person decides.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-handoff-code-file] `<ID>.values.applied.yaml` and `<ID>.values.stale.yaml` are written by code only. Door: write your fields to `<ID>.values.yaml`.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-handoff-edit-pending] A handover form is not edited while its `<ID>.values.yaml` waits to be applied. Door: put the field into `<ID>.values.yaml` (rewrite it whole with the field added).
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-handoff-rewrite] A handover form that exists is never rewritten whole by Write. Door: Write `work/handoffs/<ID>.values.yaml` with `path: value` lines, or Edit one field.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-handoff-values] A Write of `<ID>.values.yaml` lands only when the form with those values merged is ready (every word from its list, every line parses, every path known), or when it fills `blocked.problem`. Door: rewrite the file with the kept lines and the fixed lines the refusal lists; what you cannot fill goes to `blocked.field` and `blocked.problem`.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-human-word] A role never runs a command that records a person's word: `waiver.py --stage` or `--carry-from`, `ticket_adapter.py accept-gap` or `review --record`, `source_exclusions.py --load` or `--revoke`, `stand_identity.py record|confirm|forget|unconfirm`, `environment_record.py record|revoke`, `project_knowledge.py account|role|revoke|side|lesson`, `report_adapt.py kind|forget`, `story_step.py decide`. Door: return the open point in your digest.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-logs] An evidence `.log` or `.junit.xml` heavier than `guards.raw_log_free_bytes` (default 8192 bytes) is never read whole, by Read or by a shell command (a command that mentions `run_suite` is exempt). Door: read the `<label>-<ts>.json` summary beside the log (`error_head`, failed names); with a shell, `run_suite.py --request <file> --detail <test>`.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-owner] An artifact owned by a role is written only by that role, or while a dispatch of that role is open for the story. Door: name it in your digest; the conductor sends it back to its owner (`controller.py --operation rework`).
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-patch-unchecked] A write whose content the guard can read; a patch it cannot parse is blocked. Door: a patch in the host's grammar (`*** Begin Patch` / `*** End Patch`, a path per section).
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-plugin-read] A role's Read, Grep or Glob never targets the installed plugin outside its `references/` folder. Door: read your brief `work/briefs/<ID>.md` and the plugin's `references/`.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-stand-record-write] A role never writes `records/stand-identity.json`, `records/environment-properties.json`, `records/report-adaptations.json`, `records/project-knowledge.json` or a story's `state/stand-confirmations.jsonl`. Door: hand off as a halt with the row `stand · blocked · <what>` and the evidence line in `blocked`.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-unparsed-event] (No requirement the role can meet: the host's hook event could not be read.). Door: try the call once more; the second time the factory records a finding and the conductor is called.
- [guard_pre_tool:PT-walker-error] A shell command is one the guard's command reader can walk. Door: several simpler commands, or the long text written to a file with Write.
- [handoff_check:blocked_problem] A row in state `blocked` carries `blocked.problem`; `blocked_by_env` is used only where `options_for_role` offers it to this role. Door: write the problem, or pick a state the role is offered.
- [handoff_check:claims] What the form claims is true is true on disk ("the form claims this is true, and it is not"). Door: fix the claim or make it true.
- [handoff_check:cli] The call names an existing UTF-8 form with a `contract:` line and an existing values file; `--shorten` only with `--fix`. Door: the refusal's door; a non-UTF-8 form: run `handoff_init` again (:3040-3041).
- [handoff_check:field.blank] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page) Door: write the value as a `path: value` line in the values file, then run the check again.
- [handoff_check:field.max_len] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page) Door: shorten it (`--shorten` with `--fix`) or rewrite.
- [handoff_check:field.value] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page) Door: write one of the listed words (or `new: <word> -- <why>` where the list is open).
- [handoff_check:findings_tooling] A finding whose cause is `tooling` is repeated in `tooling_findings`. Door: add it to `tooling_findings`.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.failures] Each shown failure has a triage row. Door: triage it once.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.listing] Everything named in `listed_in` exists, and nothing extra stands. Door: list exactly what exists.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.names] Every row has a name. Door: name the row.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.repairs] No repair is pending when the null outcome is claimed. Door: finish or record the repair.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.report] The run report is readable. Door: rerun / point at the readable report.
- [handoff_check:null_outcome.verdict] The triage verdict is a known word. Door: write a known verdict.
- [handoff_check:required_rows] A required list has one row per item in scope: the id, a state and a reason of at most 80 characters. Door: write the rows as index lines in the values file, then run this check again.
- [handoff_check:required_rows.null_word] A list's null-outcome word (the declared empty outcome) stands only when the list has no rows; never both. Door: remove the word or remove the rows.
- [handoff_check:required_rows.owed_by_verdict] When the verdict owes rows (the verdict word names work done on items), the list is not empty. Door: write the rows the verdict owes, or change the verdict.
- [handoff_check:tried] In a contract that asks what was tried (TRIED_CONTRACTS), each tried entry states what was tried and the error it gave (TRIED_MEANING). Door: fill the tried entry with the attempt and its error.
- [handoff_check:values_apply] Each path names a field of this contract, by its index where it is a list row, not a contract-owned path; a list field gets a list and a one-value field one value; rows open in order. Door: correct the path (the refusal suggests "did you mean").
- [handoff_check:values_file] The values file is `path: value` lines (or a JSON object): valid JSON, an object not a list, each path given once, each key a field path, no nested value. Door: fix the line the refusal names (FILE_FIX).
- [host_adapter:HA-call-shape] A tool call has a shape the host adapter can read (a command as text or an argv list, one call per code cell, no tty option). Door: send the command as text or as an argv list.
- [host_adapter:HA-connector-orchestrator] A caller with a shell never calls a connector tool that `host_tools.read_only` does not list. Door: name it in your digest; the conductor registers a verified read-only tool.
- [host_adapter:HA-exec-tty] On Codex, an `exec_command` call never asks for a tty. Door: a non-interactive call.
- [host_adapter:HA-no-command-text] On Codex, every command call carries its command text (the field words of FIELD_WORDS; in a code cell, the literal `tools.exec_command({cmd: ...})`). Door: send the command in the fields the refusal names.
- [host_adapter:HA-role-nested-delegation] On Codex, a role with its own agent file does not delegate to another agent. Door: name the need in your digest; the conductor dispatches.
- [host_adapter:HA-stdin-chars] On Codex, a `write_stdin` call never sends characters to a running process. Door: a guarded `exec_command` call.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.commit.manifest] A commit does not leave a manifest case unresolved without a reason from the closed vocabulary (`closed_unresolved_reasons()` or `deferred:<gate>`). Door: write the reason on the case.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.commit.pathspec] A commit names its paths (or uses `--`) and never `-a` or `--all`. Door: git commit -m "..." -- <paths>.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.delivery] Before gate B, a delivery form is written only when the ledger word is `yes` or `after_checks`, or a deliver_with_risks journal line stands. Door: write it without those words, split it, or file it.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.opaque] Inside an open dispatch, a command that launches the runner holds none of the forms the shell reads differently from the guard (`hooklib.SHELL_OPAQUE_BAN`, e.g. a backslash-escaped quote). Door: write it without that form, or launch `run_suite.py --request FILE` as its own command.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.request] The `--request` file exists (or the same command writes it), parses, and each request names the running dispatch's `dispatch_id` and selects only instances inside its scope (an instance is in scope when the manifest says it `covers` a scope case). Door: `run_suite.py --template request`; add the case to `covers` through `manifest_put.py`.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.stash] A `git stash` names its paths. Door: name the paths.
- [stage_guard:SG-command.typed_runner] Inside an open dispatch, tests run only through `run_suite.py --mine <CASE>`, `--request FILE` or `--schedule FILE`, with the runner's path and flags written literally (no `$(...)`, backtick pair or `(Join-Path ...)`); `--task/--label` and the default full suite are refused. Door: `run_suite.py --mine <CASE>`.
- [stage_guard:SG-walker-error] A shell command is one the stage guard's command reader can walk. Door: several simpler commands, or the long text written to a file.
- [exit_gate:digest] Your final message is the handoff form: a header `<role> <stage> <window> · ok|concerns|halt|impossible`; one line `<id> · <state> · <reason of at most 80 characters>` for every item of the dispatch's scope (a halting digest owes no scope lines); nothing but those lines between the header and the path; and, last, the task-relative path of what you wrote (a halting digest may omit it). A verdict or a state word outside the form's list is advice, not a refusal; a reason over 80 characters, an absolute path under the task root, prose before the header and a missing path the witness names are mended by code when mending makes the form pass. Door: fix the digest line the refusal names, then end the dispatch again.
- [execution_request:active_dispatch] A `--mine` call belongs to exactly one running dispatch: the controller of the story has one open (with `--dispatch ID`, that running dispatch or one it resumes through `parent_retry`); when several are open, `--dispatch ID` (and `--task TICKET` across stories) names yours. Door: pass `--dispatch <your prompt's Dispatch id>` (and `--task <T>`); when none is open, name it in your digest (the conductor opens dispatches).
- [execution_request:case_entries] An asked case id names one case: a bare id the story holds under more than one area is asked with its area (`<area>/<id>`), and the manifest row's `covers` names the same area as the dispatch scope (a row that names no area is not run for a qualified id when the story holds the number under several areas, or once another row names one). Door: `--mine <area>/<id>`; or correct the row's `covers` through `manifest_put.py`; or hand the case back in your digest.
- [execution_request:mine_call] A `--mine` call names at least one case id (in the project's case-id form), a `--purpose` of `initial`, `repair_verify` or `red_probe` (any other purpose goes through `--request`), `--node-id` only with ONE case, at most one of `--cwd` and `--sandbox-root`, and a red probe always one of them (never the author's tree). Door: correct the call as the refusal names (`--template request` for another purpose; `red_sandbox.py --probe` prepares and passes the sandbox).
- [execution_request:no_test] Every asked case has a test to run: a manifest row with file and selector, or (pytest only) a file the manifest names whose tests mention the case in a marker, comment or docstring. Door: put the test in the manifest through `manifest_put.py` (file + selector), or name it for this run: `--mine <case> --node-id <file>::<test function>`.
- [execution_request:place_rows] Every test file the manifest names for an asked case exists under the run directory or the project root (a path relative to the project root). Door: correct `file` through `manifest_put.py` (path relative to the project root), or pass `--cwd` when the test lives in a sandbox.
- [execution_request:profile] The execution profile of the run is known without a guess: a profile named by `--profile` or a manifest row's `profile_id` is one `qa-factory/config.json` holds; the asked cases run under one profile; a row that names no profile and whose file lies under another profile's test root, or a root several profiles share, names its `profile_id`; when nothing else tells, `--profile` names it. Door: `profile_id` on the manifest row through `manifest_put.py --fragment`, or `--profile ID` (only where the caller takes it: `run_suite --mine`, never `probe_by_code`, :1707-1708, :1728); cases of two profiles: one `--mine` per profile.
- [execution_request:profile_command] The profile's one-test command in `qa-factory/config.json` is readable: `commands.one_test.argv` present and in shape, its `env` in shape, and a `selectors.join` rule (when the profile has one) of the form `{"option", "separator", "group"?}`. Door: report it in your digest as an onboarding gap, and write this one run with `run_suite.py --template request`.
- [execution_request:scope] A dispatch runs only the cases it was given: every asked case is in the dispatch's scope (a stale live check of a qa-code-critic red probe is admitted by code; anything else passes only on a person's recorded word). Door: hand the case back in your digest; the conductor dispatches it or records the person's word (`waiver.py`, block "outside its scope").
- [execution_request:selector_args] A manifest row of a profile that does not run pytest carries `selector_args` (the framework's own arguments) and `report_test_id`, unless the factory can build the selection from a `run_forms` direct form. Door: give the row `selector_args` and `report_test_id` through `manifest_put.py` once; until then run through `--template request`.
- [execution_request:stand] The stand the run would stand on can be looked at now, and it runs this story's build. Door: name it as `environment` in your digest (`stand_health.py --probe --env <environment>`); a stand that runs another build: the person's word at the build question of the stage entry.
- [execution_request:stand.probe] The story's first typed run on a profile has a way to identify the stand: an `execution.runtime_probes` entry for the profile (or `*`) with an `argv`, or an earlier typed run of the story on the profile to copy the probe from. Door: the probe write command the refusal prints when there is one (`runtime_probe.py --suggest --write --profile <p>`), else write this one request from `run_suite.py --template request` (every later `--mine` copies its probe).
- [execution_request:stand.reference] The story's record does not name its own stand (`pipeline.json` `environment`) as the reference (old version) of a side as well. Door: tell the conductor in your digest which stand runs the new version (the record is corrected by `stage_done.py --set sides.<side>.reference=...`, a conductor command - F-W2).
- [execution_request:window_first] A run that picks part of a case (`--node-id`) does not leave tests of the same file in the dispatch's scope that have never run in this window: one call runs them together. Door: run the command the answer names (`run_suite.py --mine <cases>`); only what a repair touched: `--purpose repair_verify`; this exact run once more: `--again`.
- [role_cli:execution_fingerprint.py] the ONE argument is a path to your fingerprint specification file, never JSON on the command line. The file carries all six, and the command names every one missing, each file by its list and position (test_files[2]): source_revision (the revision the tests ran against), test_files, config_files, dependency_files (each a list of paths or {path, sha256} records (helper_files optional) for files that exist on disk now), runtime_provenance (an object: the verified stand-identity record the runner wrote, read whole by the same check that judges a stand record; it carries profile_id, timestamp (ISO-8601), environment_id, expected_source_revision, result, observed_runtime_identity (not needed when result is not_applicable) and evidence_refs (a list, non-empty when result is matched); result `matched` also needs provenance.technical_verification true and provenance.source_linkage exact or verified_content; `matched`, `person_confirmed` and `not_applicable` are fingerprinted, `unknown` and `mismatched` are refused), profile_id (the profile the run belongs to). project_config is optional: the path of qa-factory/config.json, one of the config_files; with it config_sha hashes only that profile's execution-relevant configuration (references/config-projection.json), and without it every config file is hashed whole. The hashes are read from disk and compared - a claimed sha256 that is not its 64-hex digest is refused, a claimed sha256 that does not match the bytes is refused, and so is a file that is not there.; how to prove it: the command prints the fingerprint it computed; a mismatch names the file whose bytes changed, so prior evidence for that file is stale and its tests re-run. Door: write the input the command asks for as its refusal names it, then run the same command again.
- [run_suite:begin] A request's `idempotency_key` is new, or names the very request (same digest) already recorded under it; a key another process is claiming at the same moment is not reused. Door: write the request with a new `idempotency_key` (a `--mine` run takes a key of its own: run it again); a claim that cannot be read: `--recover <key> --task <T>`.
- [run_suite:recover] `--recover <KEY> --task <T>` names the idempotency key of a job recorded in that story's job store, and the job's file is readable JSON. Door: the `idempotency_key` the earlier answer printed (the not-launched answer names `--recover <idempotency_key> --task <task>`, `run_suite.py:3026-3027`) and your prompt's task; a job file that cannot be read is the factory's: name it in your digest.
- [validate_artifacts:check_remedy_rows] A row blocked on the environment carries a `remedy` that is the fix, and names no value of a credential key. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [role_cli:first_look.py put] --task-root <T> --file <rows.yaml>: your first look, written ONCE after you walked the survey place. The file is block YAML, `rows:` with one mapping per requirement of the register (no row missing, none outside it): req (R-n), status (confirms | contradicts | missing | unreachable), blocked_by (product | access | nature; ONLY on a missing or unreachable row, never on confirms or contradicts), why (what you did and saw), evidence (a list of capture paths of THIS walk, as the walk commands printed them) and quote (words copied from those captures); only a `blocked_by: nature` row may cite no capture. Optional: path (url, steps, locators, api, data, roles, stand_needs) and a top-level `gaps:` list. The walk, the stand, the time and the heads are written by the code; whatever you send for them is ignored. There is no --null for you: the driver records an empty outcome.; how to prove it: the printed JSON says written true and the number of rows; a refusal (exit 2) lists every problem with its door, and writes nothing - fix the file and call again, or record what you saw as a gap in your handover and halt when it says the walk is not open or the code or register changed. Door: write the input the command asks for as its refusal names it, then run the same command again.

- [run_suite:reparse] A reparse names an existing task-local run block by its canonical immutable block_id, with machine reporter evidence whose raw file is present, safe and unchanged; a mapping (needs instance_contracts) covers exactly the prior selected instances, with reporter ids non-empty and unique, and no projection collision. - [validate_artifacts:check_run_report_coverage] Every case S5 automated and every manual-agent plan row is accounted for in the run report. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_run_report_empty] A run with zero tests carries `env_preflight: blocked`, or names its environment-blocked, manual-check or manual-skipped rows. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_run_report_head] The run report carries a non-empty `head`. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_run_report_v0] The run report carries an `execution_status` from its list, computed from the run's own evidence, and `blocked` when `env_preflight` is blocked. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.

### Only in a first look (replaces "Not in a first look")

- [first_look:put.input] The input file is readable in the first-look form. Door: fix the input file.
- [first_look:put.inputs_current] The code and the register the first look was taken on are still the current ones. Door: take the first look again on the current code/register.
- [first_look:put.null_reason] A null first look carries a reason from the closed list. Door: write one of the listed reasons.
- [first_look:put.rows] Each row states its path, API, auth and locator correctly (sub-ids below from the problem builders). Door: fix the row the problem names.
- [first_look:put.rows.api] An API entry names method and route. Door: correct it.
- [first_look:put.rows.auth] An auth entry names how access is got. Door: correct it.
- [first_look:put.rows.list] A list field is a list. Door: write it as a list.
- [first_look:put.rows.locator] A locator is in the accepted form. Door: correct it.
- [first_look:put.rows.path] A path names a real place of the product. Door: correct it.
- [first_look:put.rows.row] Each row has its required fields. Door: fill them.
- [first_look:put.walk_open] A first look is put only while its walk is open. Door: open the walk first (the refusal's command).

### Not yet in rows

work/run-report.json is read field by field. `witness` at least 30 characters naming the run_suite summary that EXISTS on disk (evidence/<label>-<ts>.json) with the exit code and the totals line - a retelling is not a witness. `head` non-empty: evidence not bound to a sha goes stale. `env_preflight` pass|blocked, and blocked means `execution_status` is env_blocked - one field, one source. `execution_status` from passed|failed|env_blocked|not_executed|broken_run|timeout. `totals` an object. Every `results[]` row names ONE case, even when one test covers several, with a status from passed|failed|error|skipped|not_run, and a skip carries its reason; `manual_checks[].result` is pass|fail|inconclusive; a manual `build` takes a `--then-quote` per Then (`thens`). Empty is not clean: a zero run with env_preflight pass and no env_blocked, manual_checks or manual_skipped is refused - return blocked with a reason instead. And every case S5 automated, plus every manual-agent row of the plan, has to appear in some lane of this report: results, manual_checks, skipped, impossible, env_blocked, manual_skipped or manual_human. Where a case went is your call; saying nothing about it is not.
